description: The fifth burned pin: a fresh run must not stamp B9C_SHA256/B9A_SHA256, and verify must enforce the WAL-invariant ROW-CONTENT digest rather than the file byte hash. Each mutant reverts one fresh path to burned-byte behaviour -- fresh stamping falls back to the constant, verify enforces bytes again, the content-change guard or the no-content-digest guard is dropped, or resume compares bytes -- and dies against fixtures where the byte hash moved but the rows did not, or the rows changed.

mutants.name: fresh stamping falls back to the burned constant
mutants.note: A fresh run returns the burned-constant identity with no content digest; test_a_fresh_run_records_the_declared_content_digest_not_the_burned_constant fails (no b9c_content_sha256).

mutants.name: the no-content-digest refusal is removed
mutants.note: A fresh source declaring no row-content digest is pinned anyway instead of refused; test_a_fresh_source_without_a_content_digest_is_refused fails.

mutants.name: verify reverts to enforcing the byte hash
mutants.note: Fresh verify enforces file bytes again, so a checkpoint that moved the bytes refuses; test_verify_passes_when_only_the_bytes_moved fails.

mutants.name: the content-change check no longer refuses
mutants.note: A genuine change to the source's rows is admitted; test_verify_refuses_a_content_change fails.

mutants.name: resume compares bytes, not content, in fresh mode
mutants.note: Fresh resume compares the byte hash, so a checkpoint between attempts strands a correct resume; test_resume_survives_a_byte_only_change_but_refuses_a_content_change fails.

expected_survivors_note: None. Each mutant reverts one fresh path to burned-byte behaviour and is killed by FreshSourcePinIsWalInvariantTests, whose fixtures separate a moved byte hash (must pass) from a changed row-content digest (must refuse). Burned-mode behaviour is unchanged and covered by the existing source/resume tests.
pytest_args_reason: Scoped to FreshSourcePinIsWalInvariantTests, which drives source_identity/verify_source_artifacts/assert_resumable with in-memory and small on-disk fixtures and needs no external artifact. The burned-path source tests (PublicationGateTests, the ResumeTests) open research/b9c_signature_inventory.sqlite -- the burned inventory, an UNTRACKED evidence artifact absent from the sweep's tracked-only staged tree -- so they cannot run there and the unmutated baseline would fail on them, exactly as b9d_fresh_cutoff.sweep.json documents. Every declared mutant reverts a FRESH path and is killed by a FreshSourcePin case; the burned path is unchanged and covered by those tests in the full working-tree suite. COST, per the framework's rule: a mutant killable only through an excluded burned test would report as a survivor here and must earn an in-memory test rather than a declaration -- none of these are, they are all fresh-path.
